mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the Federal Funds rate above 3.5% for three consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 3.5% and remains above for 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant negative relationship with the FEDFUNDS rate change (p > 0.05 in OLS), or the rate increase is not sustained for three months.

mechanism_narrative: Rising employment momentum as measured by PAYEMS (monthly payrolls) coincides with stronger consumer confidence and higher S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days, especially when unemployment falls below 4.5%.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS crosses above 140,000 and remains above for 2 months
failure_condition: In periods with falling PAYEMS, 20-day forward returns are not positively correlated with PAYEMS growth (Pearson's rho < 0.2).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in industrial production (INDPRO) followed by a decline in consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) suggests supply-side strength that boosts investor confidence, driving positive S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO crosses above 115 and CPIAUCSL declines by >2% in the following month
failure_condition: No significant correlation between INDPRO movement and SPX 5-day returns (Granger causality fails at 5% level).

mechanism_narrative: A multi-month surge in residential housing starts (HOUST) indicates improving building activity and reduced supply constraints, which are associated with positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns during non-recessionary regimes.
candidate_trigger: HOUST crosses above 1,000 and remains above for 4 months
failure_condition: During periods of declining HOUST, 20-day forward returns are not higher than average (median return = 0%).

mechanism_narrative: Persistent declines in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% signal labor market tightness that supports higher equity valuations, predicting positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses below 4% and remains below for 6 months
failure_condition: UNRATE remains above 4% for 12 months with no significant positive SPX 60-day returns (t-test, p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in consumer payrolls (PAYEMS) followed by a rebound suggests labor market weakness that initially depresses sentiment but is quickly offset by optimism about recovery, yielding positive 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS crosses below 130,000 and then rises by >10,000 in the next month
failure_condition: No statistically significant positive return in the 20 days following PAYEMS declines (t-test, p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in industrial production (INDPRO) above 120 for three consecutive months accompanied by falling consumer prices (CPIAUCSL) indicates robust supply growth and disinflation, which drive negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns due to over-optimism.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 120 for 3 months and CPIAUCSL < 210 for 2 months
regime_hint: robust supply growth with deflationary signals
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns remain positive despite the signal (p > 0.05 in regression).

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly inflation rate (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 2.5% for two consecutive months while the federal funds rate remains unchanged, it creates policy divergence that is associated with negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 2.5% and remains above for 2 months with FEDFUNDS unchanged
failure_condition: Inflation above 2.5% is not associated with negative 20-day forward returns (p > 0.10 in OLS).
